note: One note game turned three ways on the low E and A strings: find the named note and play it into the mic, say the lit note's name before pressing it, then tap every place one note sits. Each step names the control as the screen shows it (Playing it (mic), Start) and who acts (the game); each block has one extra line: a feel to reach, what to do when a name won't come, or the sense it trains. Folds in the four first-week files of the same game.

exercise.title: Notes on the low E and A strings
exercise.why: A chord shape moved up the neck is named by the note under it on the low E or the A string, so knowing these notes lets you name any chord you move.

cells.text:
Press Playing it (mic) under the neck below. Then press Start above the neck.
The game names a note and a string: find it on your guitar and play it, saying its name out loud. The game hears your answer.
Practice until your finger goes to some of the notes without counting frets from the open string.

Press Start in the game below. Now the game lights a note on the neck: say its name out loud first, then press that name under the neck to check.
Play the note on your guitar as you answer, so your hand learns the place while your eyes learn the name.

Press Start in the game below. The game names a note: tap every place it sits on the two strings, then play those places on your guitar, low to high.
Notice which notes your finger goes to at once: the ones you still count up to are the ones to practice next.
